advances: Three positive continuous fibers, prescribed genuine minimizing caps and fixed mark. The outer comparison uses the support simplex in those same directions.

proof:
Write $a=|A|,k=|K|,b=|B|$. The actual mixed measure is the sum of ordinary $d$-volumes on the three disjoint isometric fibers. Convexity gives $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let $U_i$ be the volume of the $A$ trace $v_i\cdot x\ge-1$. The $B$ trace $v_i\cdot x\ge1$ has zero volume by $B\subseteq T$ and the null hyperplane boundary. Thus the middle trace has volume $Q-U_i$. The middle traces $v_i\cdot x\ge0$ cover $\mathbb R^d$ because the evaluations sum to zero. One trace contains the ordinary centroid of $K$, so fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d at full mass gives $Q\ge\Gamma k$. With $y=0$, continuous normal $v_i$ and integer coefficient $-1$, each listed ambient cap satisfies the hypotheses of the fixed-normal tilt lemma 03c59c70402b66a2. It gives $U_i\le2(Q-U_i)$, hence $U_i\le2Q/3$.

For $d\ge2$, sort $U_1\le\cdots\le U_{d+1}$, relabeling only for the following computation. The $A$ traces also cover $\mathbb R^d$, since some evaluation is nonnegative at every point. Use the uniform-volume three-largest-cap inequality of ac7ba1e1e0ebc955 separately on $A$ and $K$, each with its actual finite cover. With $\kappa=1/\Gamma-2\in(0,1)$ and $l=d+1$, the two inequalities are
$$
 a\le U_l+U_{l-1}+\kappa U_{l-2},
 \qquad k\le Q/\Gamma-U_1-U_2-\kappa U_3.
$$
The excess of their sum over $Q/\Gamma$ is bounded, respectively for $d=2,3,4$, by $(1-\kappa)U_l$, $(2-\kappa)U_l$, $2U_l$. Indeed the respective differences in the cap terms are $(1-\kappa)(U_3-U_1)$, $(U_4-U_1)+(1-\kappa)(U_3-U_2)$, and $U_5+U_4-U_1-U_2$. In $d\ge5$ bound the three positive terms by $(2+\kappa)U_l=U_l/\Gamma$ and drop the three subtractions. With $U_l\le2Q/3$ these yield $a+k\le Q/\Gamma+C_dQ$, where
$$
 C_2=1/2,\qquad C_3=88/81,\qquad C_4=4/3,\qquad C_d=2/(3\Gamma)\quad(d\ge5).
$$

If $K$ is aligned, apply the sharp volume credit to the actual triple, obtaining $b<\rho_d k\le \rho_d Q/\Gamma$. For $d\ge2$ this gives $W/Q<(1+\rho_d)/\Gamma+C_d$. Substituting the exact intersection values gives the stated bounds $4/17,81/376,768/3589$. They exceed $\Gamma/2$ respectively because $4/17>2/9$, $81/376>27/128$, and $1+\rho_4+(4/3)\Gamma=3589/1875<2$. For $d\ge5$ the ratio bound has denominator $5/3+\rho_d<2$ by the uniform simplex intersection estimate. In $d=1$ the two opposite middle traces partition $K$ up to their common point, whereas the two $A$ traces cover $A$. The two zero $B$-volume identities give $a+k\le2Q$. Here $\rho_1=1$, so the aligned credit gives $b<k\le2Q$ and $W<4Q$.

If $K$ is arbitrary, $\overline K$ contains $K$ and is an aligned simplex. Indeed the support values have positive mean by testing strict supports at an interior point, and the evaluation map identifies the displayed inequalities with a positive dilation and translation of $-T$. Thus the midpoint inclusion and proper endpoint cuts allow the sharp volume credit with middle body $\overline K$, giving $|\overline K|>b/\rho_d$. All cap-profile bounds still refer to the actual $K$. Under the bad-target hypothesis,
$$
 2Q/\Gamma\le W\le b+Q/\Gamma+C_d Q,\qquad
 k\le Q/\Gamma\le b/(1-\Gamma C_d).
$$
The four denominators $1-\Gamma C_d$ are $7/9,13/24,851/1875,1/3$ respectively for $d=2,3,4,\ge5$. Dividing by the strict lower bound on $|\overline K|$ gives exactly the asserted deficits.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let the only nonempty integer fibers of a compact convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies $A,K,B$ at $-1,0,1$. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_{d+1}$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and sum to zero, and put $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1\ \forall i\}$ and $\rho_d=|T\cap(-T)|/|T|$. Suppose $B\subseteq T$, $0\in\operatorname{int} K$, every $v_i\cdot x=-1$ meets $\operatorname{int}A$, and all closed ambient caps $v_i\cdot x\ge z$ attain the genuine raw depth $Q$ at the point $(0,0)$. Let $\Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $W=|A|+|K|+|B|$.

If $K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-t_i\ \forall i\}$, the normalized depth $Q/W$ is strictly greater than $\Gamma/2$. More precisely, the strict lower bounds in dimensions $1,2,3,4$ are $1/4,4/17,81/376,768/3589$, respectively, and the bound for $d\ge5$ is $\Gamma/(5/3+\rho_d)$.

For an arbitrary such $K$, put $\overline K=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge-h_K(-v_i)\ \forall i\}$. For $d\ge2$, if $Q\le\Gamma W/2$, then the strict upper bounds on $|K|/|\overline K|$ in dimensions $2,3,4$ are $6/7,12/13,690/851$, respectively. For $d\ge5$ the ratio is strictly below $3\rho_d<1$.
title: Marked depth with an aligned simplex middle fiber and necessary outer simplex deficits
